questions.question: In 1994, Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes set fire to the home of which NFL star — beginning one of R&B's most publicized personal crises?

metadata.fact: Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes set fire to Andre Rison's mansion in Atlanta in June 1994 — she later said she intended to burn only his shoes, which she had placed in a bathtub, but the fire spread to the entire home. Rison, a wide receiver who played for the Atlanta Falcons, did not press criminal charges. Lopes entered rehab and received five years of supervised probation.
metadata.storyHook: She meant to burn his shoes. The bathtub fire spread. The whole house went. Andre Rison didn't press charges. TLC's biggest album was still coming.
metadata.sourceNotes: Fulton County court records (1994). Atlanta Journal-Constitution archival coverage. TLC biographical records.

questions.question: Mariah Carey's 2001 public breakdown occurred while she was promoting which album — widely considered one of the decade's biggest commercial disasters?

metadata.fact: 'Glitter' — the soundtrack to Mariah Carey's semi-autobiographical film — was released September 11, 2001, a date that ensured minimal promotional coverage. The album debuted at #7 on the Billboard 200 and quickly fell. Months of erratic public appearances preceded its release, culminating in a July 2001 TRL appearance that became one of the era's most widely covered celebrity incidents.
metadata.storyHook: The album dropped on September 11, 2001. No promotional cycle survived that date. The breakdown had already happened by then. 'Glitter' arrived into silence.
metadata.sourceNotes: Glitter liner notes (Virgin Records, 2001). Billboard 200 chart archives. TRL broadcast archives (July 2001).

questions.question: MC Hammer filed for bankruptcy in 1996 — his reported liabilities at the time were approximately how much?

metadata.fact: MC Hammer filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in April 1996 with approximately $13 million in liabilities against $1 million in assets — a collapse driven by a payroll of roughly 200 employees, a $12 million mansion in Fremont, California, and spending habits built around a commercial peak that ended faster than it arrived.
metadata.storyHook: Earned over $33 million. Spent most of it on 200 employees and a mansion. Filed for bankruptcy at $13 million in the red. The math is a cautionary tale that still gets taught in business schools.
metadata.sourceNotes: MC Hammer Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing (1996). US Bankruptcy Court documentation. Billboard chart archives.

questions.question: Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes died in April 2002 while traveling in which Central American country?

metadata.fact: Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes died on April 25, 2002, in La Ceiba, Honduras — she was involved in a car accident while riding in an SUV with members of her entourage. She was in Honduras working with herbalist Alfredo Bowman and filming a personal documentary. She was 30 years old.
metadata.storyHook: She was 30 years old. Filming a documentary. Riding in an SUV in Honduras. The accident came from nowhere. TLC had one member fewer, and the industry had one of its most startling losses.
metadata.sourceNotes: La Ceiba, Honduras accident report (April 25, 2002). TLC biographical records. Documentary production documentation.

questions.question: D'Angelo returned from his long absence from music with which 2014 comeback album — released as a surprise with minimal advance notice?

metadata.fact: 'Black Messiah' was released on December 15, 2014, with roughly 24 hours of advance notice — D'Angelo's first studio album in fourteen years arrived during a moment of significant social unrest in the United States, and its content reflected the political tenor of the moment. The album received unanimous critical acclaim and won the Grammy for Best R&B Album.
metadata.storyHook: Fourteen years of silence. A 24-hour announcement. December 15, 2014. 'Black Messiah' arrived during a week of national protest and landed as one of the most politically charged R&B records in decades.
metadata.sourceNotes: Black Messiah liner notes (RCA Records, 2014). Billboard chart archives. Grammy Award records.

questions.question: Aaliyah died in August 2001 immediately after completing the music video for which song?

metadata.fact: Aaliyah completed filming the 'Rock the Boat' video in the Bahamas on August 24, 2001 — she and eight others died the following day when their chartered Cessna 402 crashed shortly after takeoff from Marsh Harbour Airport on Abaco Island. She was 22 years old. 'Rock the Boat' was released posthumously.
metadata.storyHook: She finished filming on a Friday. The plane crashed Saturday morning. The video was released after her death. 'Rock the Boat' is inseparable from what happened the morning after it was completed.

questions.question: TLC's manager — who had signed them to a contract with an unfavorable royalty structure that left each member earning very little per album sold — was known by which stage name?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — TLC'S MANAGER'S STAGE NAME

metadata.fact: Pebbles — born Perri Arnette McKissack, later Perri Reid — managed TLC and was married to LaFace Records co-founder L.A. Reid at the time of the signing, creating a significant conflict of interest. TLC's original contract reportedly paid the entire group approximately 56 cents per album sold — split three ways and eaten further by recoupable expenses, each member was clearing less than 19 cents per unit before costs. Despite becoming the best-selling female group in American history, they filed for bankruptcy in 1995 while CrazySexyCool was at its commercial peak.
metadata.storyHook: The manager was married to the label head. The contract paid the entire group 56 cents per album — split three ways, less than 19 cents each before expenses. The album became the best-selling female group record in American history. The artists filed for bankruptcy anyway.
metadata.sourceNotes: TLC bankruptcy filing (1995). Perri Reid management documentation. LaFace Records conflict-of-interest documentation. Billboard chart archives.

questions.question: Andre Rison — whose home Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes burned down in 1994 — played which position in the NFL?

metadata.fact: Andre Rison was a wide receiver who played for multiple NFL teams — including the Atlanta Falcons at the time of the 1994 fire — and was known as one of the era's most electrifying pass-catchers. His relationship with Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes was public knowledge before the fire, and the incident generated coverage that spanned sports and entertainment media simultaneously.
metadata.storyHook: An R&B star. An NFL wide receiver. A house fire. 1994 was the year the sports and entertainment tabloid worlds became one story.

questions.question: D'Angelo's 2005 arrest for DWI and drug possession — which extended his already-ongoing hiatus — occurred in which state?

metadata.fact: D'Angelo was arrested in Virginia in January 2005 for DWI and drug possession — he had already been largely absent from public life since the end of the Voodoo tour in 2000-2001, a retreat driven partly by the intense physical objectification that followed the 'Untitled (How Does It Feel)' video. The 2005 arrest deepened and extended the hiatus, ultimately lasting until Black Messiah's surprise release in December 2014.
metadata.storyHook: The initial retreat started in 2000 after the Voodoo tour. The 2005 arrest in Virginia came during an already-ongoing silence. By then D'Angelo had been gone for five years, and the arrest ensured he would be gone for nine more.
metadata.sourceNotes: Virginia court records (January 2005). D'Angelo biographical records. Voodoo tour documentation (2000-2001).

questions.question: MC Hammer's financial collapse was linked partly to his extravagant compound — built in which California city near Oakland?

metadata.fact: MC Hammer built a 33,000-square-foot compound in Fremont, California — estimated to have cost around $12 million — that included a recording studio, full professional basketball court, and capacity to house his large entourage. The compound's upkeep, combined with a payroll of roughly 200 employees, consumed the earnings from his commercial peak faster than he could generate new revenue.
metadata.storyHook: Thirty-three thousand square feet. A basketball court. Two hundred employees. Twelve million dollars in construction. Fremont, California. MC Hammer built something that no single artist's career could sustain.
metadata.sourceNotes: MC Hammer bankruptcy filing documentation (1996). Fremont, California property records. Biographical accounts of compound specifications.

questions.question: Bobby Brown and Whitney Houston's turbulent marriage ended when their divorce was finalized in which year?

metadata.fact: Bobby Brown and Whitney Houston married on July 18, 1992, and divorced on April 24, 2007 — a fifteen-year marriage documented extensively in tabloid media and later in their own reality television series 'Being Bobby Brown' (2005). Their divorce preceded Whitney Houston's musical comeback period and Bobby Brown's continued public struggles.
metadata.storyHook: Married in 1992. Divorced in 2007. Fifteen years. A reality show. The marriage was one of the most documented relationships in 90s celebrity culture, and the divorce ended a chapter that had started when both artists were at their commercial peak.
metadata.sourceNotes: Georgia divorce court records (April 24, 2007). Bobby Brown and Whitney Houston biographical records.

questions.question: Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes traveled to Honduras to work with which herbalist — whose alternative medicine practices she had become devoted to in the years before her death?

metadata.fact: Alfredo Bowman — known as Dr. Sebi — was a Honduran herbalist and self-described healer whose approach to natural medicine attracted a significant following among artists and celebrities. Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes had become devoted to his practices and traveled to Honduras specifically to work with him and document the experience. She died in a car accident there on April 25, 2002.
metadata.storyHook: She traveled to a country specifically to work with a healer. The documentary she was filming recorded the days before her death. The footage was released posthumously. Honduras was not incidental — it was the destination.

reserve.question: New Edition — the group Bobby Brown rose to fame with before his solo career — formed in which Boston neighbourhood?

metadata.fact: New Edition formed in the Roxbury neighbourhood of Boston, Massachusetts in 1978. The group — which included Bobby Brown, Ralph Tresvant, Ricky Bell, Michael Bivins, and Ronnie DeVoe — is one of the most influential R&B groups to emerge from the Boston area.
metadata.storyHook: He helped build New Edition. They pushed him out. What came next was the solo career — and everything that came with it.

questions.question: TLC's original contract reportedly paid the entire group approximately how many cents per album sold — meaning each of the three members earned less than 19 cents per unit before recoupable expenses?

metadata.fact: TLC's original contract reportedly paid the entire group approximately 56 cents per album sold — split three ways and then reduced further by recoupable studio, marketing, and tour costs, each member was left with a fraction of that figure per unit. When CrazySexyCool became the best-selling album by an American female group in history, the financial benefit accrued primarily to the label and management. They filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in July 1995.
metadata.storyHook: Fifty-six cents for all three of them. Split three ways. Then recoupable expenses. Then bankruptcy. CrazySexyCool sold four million copies in six months and each member's share of each sale was less than the cost of a phone call.
metadata.sourceNotes: TLC bankruptcy filing (1995). Contract terms as reported in court filings and biographical documentation. Billboard chart archives.

questions.question: MC Hammer at his commercial peak reportedly employed how many people on his payroll — a scale of spending that contributed directly to his 1996 bankruptcy filing?

metadata.fact: MC Hammer reportedly employed approximately 200 people at his commercial peak — including dancers, bodyguards, cooks, drivers, and personal staff — while simultaneously maintaining a 33,000-square-foot compound in Fremont, California and supporting family members. His estimated $33 million in earnings from music were consumed by this infrastructure at a pace that his declining record sales could not sustain.
metadata.storyHook: Two hundred employees. A 33,000-square-foot compound. Thirty-three million dollars earned. Thirteen million dollars in debt by 1996. The numbers tell the story without editorial comment.

questions.question: Bobby Brown's 1986 debut solo album — released the same year New Edition expelled him — was titled what?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — BOBBY BROWN'S SOLO DEBUT ALBUM TITLE

metadata.fact: 'King of Stage' was Bobby Brown's debut solo album, released in 1986 on MCA Records the same year New Edition expelled him. The album was a modest commercial performer, but it established the template for Brown's more successful follow-up 'Don't Be Cruel' (1988). The title was a statement of intent — he had just been thrown out of a group and immediately declared himself royalty.
metadata.storyHook: The group voted him out in 1986. He went solo. 'Don't Be Cruel' went eight times platinum. The expulsion was the best career decision New Edition ever made for Bobby Brown, even though they didn't make it for his benefit.
metadata.sourceNotes: King of Stage liner notes (MCA Records, 1986). Bobby Brown official discography. New Edition expulsion documentation.
